messages.subject: Name for Gaussian observation component?
parts:
Hello, I am trying to generate posterior predictions at new points for an SPDE model using inlabru:

```
posterior_predictions <- generate(
  m_bru, 
  prediction_pixels, 
  ~ (1 + site))
```

Where m_bru is my model, prediction_pixels is a SpatialPointsDataFrame with the points I want to make predictions at, and site is the name of my SPDE component.

1. It seems that the result does not include samples of the nugget or what INLA calls "Gaussian observations". Is that right?

2. If so, how do I include random draws of the Gaussian observation noise in my simulations? Is there a name for that component I can add to the formula I pass to generate?

Thanks!
Eric

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Name for Gaussian observation component?
parts:
Hi,

The prediction “formula” is a general R expression with access to the latent model components and hyperparameters, so one way to include observation randomness in predictions is to add a call to rnorm(). So something like this should do what you want:

~ Intercept + site + rnorm(numberofpredictionlocations, sd=1/sqrt(Precision_for_the_Gaussian_observations))

(Note that you have to use the explicit name for the intercept component, and not just +1, as that would literally just add the constant 1 to the expression)

Finn
